description_full: Sibanye Stillwater Limited, together with its subsidiaries, operates as a precious metals mining company in South Africa, the United States, Europe, and Australia. The company produces platinum group metals (PGMs), platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium, iridium, gold, lithium, zinc, nickel, copper, and silver. Sibanye Stillwater Limited was founded in 2013 and is headquartered in Weltevredenpark, South Africa.

financial_summary: D/B/A Sibanye-Stillwater Limite is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $6.9B market cap on $6.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -19% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 27% against a 10% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.
The company is burning through $626M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -11.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
